name: Ertuğrul
role: Thirteenth-century Anatolian leader traditionally identified as Osman I’s father
summary: Ertuğrul’s political outlook cannot be reconstructed reliably from the surviving evidence. Accounts of his life largely come from later Ottoman traditions, which do not establish his personal positions on the test’s statements.

sources.title: Ertuğrul Gazi
sources.author: Fahameddin Başar, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.usedFor: Absence from contemporary histories and the late, legendary character of biographical accounts.

sources.title: ResurReaction: Competing Visions of Turkey’s (proto) Ottoman Past in Magnificent Century and Resurrection Ertuğrul (2019)
sources.author: Josh Carney
sources.usedFor: The historical record’s sparseness and the distinction between the historical figure and modern television characterization.

sources.title: Late Ottoman chronicle extracts: the dream of Ertoğrul, in Ottoman Historical Documents, chapter I, section 1, items 1a–1b
sources.author: Anonymous Ottoman chroniclers; translated by V. L. Ménage, edited by Colin Imber
sources.usedFor: Primary evidence of later dynastic tradition, not contemporary testimony or Ertuğrul’s own words. The incompatible prophetic-dream stories do not establish his political positions.

sources.title: The puzzling coins of the earliest Ottomans and their neighbors (2019), p. 182
sources.author: Clive Foss
sources.usedFor: Problems with the coins conventionally cited as evidence of Ertuğrul’s existence.
